title: Response to Study on Long-term Economic and Social Costs of Adverse Childhood Experiences
what_it_is: Response to Study on Long-term Economic and Social Costs of Adverse Childhood Experiences

sections.label: ACEs cost study findings
sections.summary: A study by IMH and KK Hospital established a baseline of the economic and social cost of Adverse Childhood Experiences in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: Social and Family Development): Mr Speaker, the Institute of Mental Health and KK Women's and Children's Hospital conducted a study to establish a baseline of the economic and social cost of Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs) in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: The study found that the impact of such events on individuals with ACEs was higher health and productivity costs, compared to individuals with no ACE exposure.

sections.label: MSF family survey results
sections.summary: A 2023 MSF survey found 86% of Singaporeans reported a close-knit family and 85.9% reported moderate to high family resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: A 2023 MSF survey on families found that 86% of Singaporeans reported that they have a close-knit family.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for
sentences.text: The same survey found that 85.9% of families reported moderate to high family resilience scores, which means that these families would generally be able to recover from challenges together as a family unit.

sections.label: MSF support for children
sections.summary: MSF provides trauma interventions and works with partners to support children affected by abuse, incarceration, or parental divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think the principle is that practice must be informed by research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: And in the study, there were some 11 forms of ACEs that were identified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For children who have experienced abuse or neglect, MSF works with community partners and agencies to provide evidence-based trauma interventions to address the trauma as well as other behavioural and emotional needs to help them develop healthy coping mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: In terms of children who have lived with family members who are or were incarcerated, MSF works with the Singapore Prison Services on processes where social service touch points, for instance, the family service centres will be notified to provide support to family members of inmates or ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: For children whose parents are separating or divorcing, MSF has also partnered social service agencies to support these children and their parents, and this include the mandatory co-parenting programme, which helps parents make informed decisions that prioritise their child's well-being as well as to practise cooperative parenting.
